title: Path kernel: multi-threaded background path generation with live progress in the UI

body:
## The maintainer's words

2026-11-27: "make a issue for new kernel that path generation should be multi threaded."

2026-11-27, second order: "path generation should run in the background and upgrade the users UI with the progress of the generation in realtime"

## Today

- The application already generates a batch of operations in parallel. It uses `rayon` and keeps the input order (`crates/app/src/commands/operation/generate.rs`, `crates/app/src/operation/job.rs`).
- #2257 added background generation. The UI shows an overlay with the operation name, the position in the batch, the elapsed time and a Cancel button (`gen_worker::GenProgress`). The overlay does not show how much of one operation is complete.
- This issue is about the work inside one operation in the path kernel (`camcraft-pathkernel`).

## What

- Find the kernel work that is independent. Examples to examine: Z levels, separate pieces of a region, guide curve sets, entry proofs.
- Plan the independent parts on more than one thread.
- Keep the steps serial where one part reads the result of an earlier part (for example the remaining stock).

## Background run and progress

- Each path generation in the kernel runs in the background. The UI stays usable during the generation.
- The kernel reports its progress during the work. Examples: the pipeline stage, and the count of complete levels or pieces.
- The UI shows the progress and changes it in real time. The progress does not move backward.
- The kernel has no UI dependency. It reports through a value or a callback that the caller supplies.
- A progress report does not change the output.
- The CLI and MCP can ignore the progress.

## Rules

- The output is the same for each thread count: the moves, the notes, the fallbacks and the order of the refusals.
- The thread count has a limit. A batch of operations and one operation share one thread pool.
- A panic or an error in one part gives one clean refusal.
- The browser build works without threads.
- A cancel request stops the work.

## Done means

- A test shows that the UI gets progress reports before the generation ends. The final report is complete.
- A UI test shows the progress in the overlay.
- A test generates the same fixtures with 1 thread and with more threads, and the results are equal.
- The PR records the generation time with 1 thread and with more threads on the large fixtures.

Part of #4023.
